issues.description: The problem statement (UML and task text) specifies getTotalNumberOfStudents() should return an int, and the template's TODO refers to implementing this method as specified in the UML. However, the provided solution implements getTotalNumberOfStudents() to return a StudentCount object and also adds a StudentCount class. This introduces a new type not mentioned in the problem statement or template and creates a mismatch in the method's return type, which will confuse students and conflict with the expected design.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution with the UML and template by changing getTotalNumberOfStudents() in the solution to return an int (e.g., return numberOfInscribedStudents + numberOfGuestStudents) and remove the StudentCount class. Alternatively, if StudentCount is intentionally required, update the problem statement and template to document the StudentCount type and its API and include a StudentCount class in the template so students are aware of the custom return type.

issues.description: The problem statement (UML) and instructions specify getTotalNumberOfStudents(): int, i.e., the total number of students should be represented as a primitive int. The solution introduces a new StudentCount type and implements getTotalNumberOfStudents() to return a StudentCount object. This creates an identifier/API mismatch for the same conceptual entity (the total number of students) across artifacts and forces students to reconcile a new class name (StudentCount) that is not mentioned in the problem or template.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the representation of the total number of students across artifacts. Either change the solution to have getTotalNumberOfStudents() return an int (and remove or avoid using StudentCount), or update the problem statement and template to document and expect the StudentCount type consistently. Preferable fix: make getTotalNumberOfStudents() return int to match the UML and simplify student mapping.
